newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative junior minister opposes EU currency.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative junior minister opposes EU currency.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives faced another rift over Europe on Tuesday in the run-up to the May 1 general election when a junior minister veered from government policy, saying he opposed joining a single European currency.
Junior health minister John Horam said in his election manifesto he was personally against a single European currency, seemingly flouting the government's "wait and see" policy.
"I am opposed to the Euro (currency) replacing the pound sterling since this would take away more of our independence," Horam wrote.

Prime Minister John Major has consistently pushed for a "wait and see" policy, preferring to decide closer to the time if Britain would join. He also warned that ministers who did not toe the government line would be sacked.
A Conservative Party spokeswoman said the party was looking into Horam's comments but refused to speculate on whether or not Major would sack him.
"We are investigating," she told Reuters, adding that she understood Horam still supported government policy.
Horam told BBC television's Newsnight programme that if there were a referendum on a single currency he would vote against it but insisted his opinion was in line with government policy.
"My position is perfectly consistent with the government's line because the government is saying we negotiate and then decide and that is absolutely right," he said.
"I personally am opposed to a single currency but I think the right line is to stay at the negotiating table..and wait and see what happens."
The opposition Labour Party and Liberal Democrats seized on the latest Conservative rift, saying it revealed new divisions in the ruling party over Europe.
Sir David Steel, former leader of the Liberal Democrats, said Horam must go.

"John Major is the captain of the ship and what's happening is that the lifeboats on the Tory Titanic are now thinning out and the petty officers are the people leaving the bridge and climbing in first. I think he has got to make an example and has got to sack Horam," he said.

It was the second embarrassing gaffe over Europe on Tuesday for the Conservatives. Earlier, Conservative vice-chairman Angela Rumbold said in an election address to her constituency that she would not vote for a single European currency.
Labour leader Tony Blair, tipped to win the election, said Major's party would be "like ferrets in a sack" over Europe if they won.
A survey conducted by the Times newspaper found that nine ministers, including two cabinet ministers, were unofficially breaching the government's policy on the single currency.
The latest opinion polls had more bad news for the Conservatives, showing Labour consistently maintaining its double-digit lead.

The Gallup poll in the Daily Telegraph newspaper gave Labour a lead of 21 percentage points over the Conservatives who now stand at 30 percent. An ICM survey for the Guardian put Labour's margin at 14 points.
